$comment: Fernhollow's size guide: authored, guide-level advice only. It never states a product's own measurements; the standard mattress sizes are the general US standard, labelled as such. Read by the brain (backend/sizing.py) and the /size-guide page. The finder's questions and the rule that picks a size live here too, so both halves pick the same size.
title: Size guide
intro: How to choose the right size before you order: beds and bedding, vases and faux stems, rugs and curtains. Only beds, bedding, vases and faux stems come in sizes at Fernhollow; rugs and curtains are chosen by fabric, so their sections are about placement.

sections.title: Beds and bedding

sizes.standard: Standard US Queen mattress: 60 × 80 in (152 × 203 cm)
sizes.suits: Most main bedrooms and guest rooms, and couples happy to sleep close.

sizes.standard: Standard US King mattress: 76 × 80 in (193 × 203 cm)
sizes.suits: Larger bedrooms, couples who want room to spread out, or a child or a pet who joins you at night.

rules: A bed frame takes the mattress of the same name: a Queen frame for a Queen mattress, a King frame for a King.
Sheets, quilts and comforters follow the mattress, not the frame.
Leave a clear walkway of about 60 cm (2 ft) on each side you get out of bed.
A quilt or comforter one size up hangs lower over the sides of the bed; choose it only if you like that look.

sections.title: Vases and faux stems

sizes.suits: A shelf, a bedside table, a desk or a windowsill: somewhere you see it up close.
The floor, a console, a sideboard or the middle of a dining table: somewhere it is seen across the room.

rules: Pair like with like: a Small stem stands in a Small vase, a Large stem in a Large vase.
On a dining table, keep it low enough to talk over.
Groups read best in odd numbers: three Small vases of one family on a shelf.

sections.title: Rugs
sections.note: Fernhollow rugs come in one size each and are chosen by fabric. Use this to judge how a rug should sit with your sofa.

layouts.label: All legs on
layouts.text: Every leg of the sofa and chairs sits on the rug: the most pulled-together look, for a larger living room.

layouts.label: Front legs on
layouts.text: Only the front legs of the sofa and chairs rest on the rug: it ties the seating together and suits most living rooms.

layouts.label: Under the coffee table
layouts.text: The rug sits under the coffee table, clear of the sofa: for a small room, or to define a reading corner.

rules: Choose a rug a little longer than your sofa, so it frames the seating rather than hiding under it.
Leave a border of bare floor, about 30 to 45 cm (12 to 18 in), between the rug and the walls.

sections.title: Curtains
sections.note: Fernhollow curtains are chosen by fabric. Use this to decide how far they should fall and where the rod goes.

drops.label: To the sill
drops.text: Ends just above the windowsill: for kitchens, deep sills, or a window over a desk or a radiator.

drops.label: Below the sill
drops.text: Falls a hand's width below the sill: a tidy look for bedrooms and small windows.

drops.label: To the floor
drops.text: Just clears the floor: the tailored look for living rooms and bedrooms, and it makes a ceiling feel higher.

rules: Hang the rod 10 to 15 cm (4 to 6 in) above the window frame, and let it run 15 to 25 cm (6 to 10 in) past each side so the curtains open clear of the glass.
For a full look, the curtains together should be about twice the width of the window.

options.label: A bed, sheets or a quilt
Two, plus a child or a pet

questions.label: How should it sit with your sofa?

rules.why: A Queen mattress takes a Queen frame and Queen bedding.
A King mattress takes a King frame and King bedding.
In a snug room a Queen leaves you a walkway round the bed.
With a child or a pet joining you, a King gives everyone room.
Two of you in a roomy bedroom: a King gives you space and still leaves a walkway.
Sleeping alone, a Queen is plenty, even in a roomy bedroom.
A Queen suits most bedrooms and leaves room to walk round it.
On a shelf you see it up close, so Small sits right.
A bedside table needs room for a lamp and a book, so Small.
On a desk or a windowsill, Small keeps it out of the way.
A centrepiece is seen across the table, so Large; keep the stems low enough to talk over.
A console or sideboard is seen across the room, so Large.
On the floor it needs height to be seen, so Large.
